title: Boundary edge
statement: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$, taking values in $\{\pm1\}$, and let $i$ be a coordinate. A dimension edge at $i$ is a sign vector $x$ with $x_i=1$. Such an edge is a boundary edge for $f$ if $f(x)$ differs from its value at the vector obtained by flipping coordinate $i$ of $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube of dimension $n$ to $\{\pm1\}$
$i$ is a coordinate among the $n$ coordinates
$e$ is a dimension edge at $i$, so its sign vector has $i$th coordinate $1$
